title: Make the leaderboard show the real winners

blocks.text: A puzzle game shows two standings after every round: the best score, and the fewest moves anyone needed. Last release, players complained that the board named the wrong winners: in some rounds the "best score" was simply the first one played, and the "fewest moves" the last one recorded. The code that picked them was rewritten in a hurry and lost.

`Leaderboard` already streams the round's numbers into `max` and `min`. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/Leaderboard.java`, `byScore()` and `byMoves()`, which give the order each standing ranks its numbers in. About two lines in total.
The tests feed rounds in which the winner sits anywhere in the list, not only where a hand-typed test list would put it.

cases.says: the best score of a round is the highest one, and an empty round has none
the fewest moves of a puzzle is the smallest count, and a puzzle nobody solved has none
the highest score wins even when it was not the first one played
the smallest move count wins even when it was not the last one recorded

origin.section: A Method Reference Is a Lambda That Makes One Call, and the Target Type Decides What the Call Means

concepts: A method reference compiles when its call fits the target interface's method; javac does not check that the method means what the interface's contract asks for.
